intro: You're looking for an accountant who understands limited companies, probably because you've set one up or are about to, and you want someone local who can handle the filing and tax side. The search for a "limited company accountant near me" suggests you'd rather deal with someone you can meet or speak to easily, and who knows the Companies House and HMRC requirements that come with running a limited company.
need_heading: What people searching for a limited company accountant usually need
need_lead: Most people behind this search want practical help with the ongoing duties of running a limited company, not just a one-off tax return.
needs: You've recently incorporated a limited company and need to understand what accounts and returns have to be filed, and when.
You're already trading through a limited company but your current accountant isn't local or isn't giving you the attention you need.
You want someone to prepare your annual accounts for Companies House and your corporation tax return for HMRC.
You're unsure how to pay yourself efficiently through a mix of salary and dividends, and want advice on the tax consequences.
You need help with the confirmation statement and other routine filings, and want to know who is responsible for sending what.
context_heading: What to understand about limited company accounting
context: A limited company has its own filing obligations that are separate from your personal tax return. Accounts must go to Companies House and a corporation tax return to HMRC, and as a director you may also need to file a Self Assessment return. A good accountant will make clear which of these they will handle for you and which remain your responsibility.

The word "accountant" is not a protected title in the UK, so it's worth asking about professional qualifications and supervision. Titles such as Chartered Accountant, Chartered Certified Accountant and Chartered Management Accountant are protected, and every practice offering accountancy services must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes by a professional body or HMRC.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say that you're looking for an accountant for a limited company and whether the company is already trading or still dormant.
Mention where you're based and how far you're willing to travel, since you searched for someone near you.
Explain what you need help with, such as annual accounts, corporation tax, confirmation statements, payroll or director Self Assessment.
Let us know if you're behind with any filings or have received reminders from Companies House or HMRC.
Say whether you already have an accountant and, if so, whether you're looking to switch.
Include any preferences, such as wanting someone who can meet in person or who works with your particular sector.
questions: Will you prepare and file the annual accounts with Companies House and the corporation tax return with HMRC?
Do you handle director Self Assessment returns, and is that included in your quote?
Who will submit the confirmation statement each year?
Can you help me plan a tax-efficient mix of salary and dividends before the year end?
Which professional body supervises your practice for anti-money-laundering purposes, and do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
How do you handle complaints if I'm unhappy with your service?

faqs.q: Do I need an accountant who is local to me?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, but many people prefer someone they can meet face to face, especially when setting up a limited company. If you search for a limited company accountant near me, you're probably looking for that convenience, but you can also ask whether they work remotely.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a bookkeeper and an accountant for a limited company?
faqs.a: A bookkeeper typically records day-to-day transactions, while an accountant prepares the annual accounts and tax returns and can advise on tax planning. For a limited company, you need someone who can handle the statutory filings with Companies House and HMRC.

faqs.q: Can I prepare my own limited company accounts?
faqs.a: It is possible to prepare and file your own accounts and tax returns, but many directors use an accountant to avoid mistakes and to get advice on tax planning. The requirements can be complex, and penalties can apply for late filing.

faqs.q: What should I have ready when I first contact an accountant?
faqs.a: It helps to have your company registration number, recent bank statements, and any records of income and expenses. If you're switching accountants, have your latest accounts and tax returns to hand.
